191 @cli.command()
192 @click.option('--model', default=None, help='The model to use for the chat.')
193 @click.option('--build_mem', is_flag=True, help='Build and enable the local memory for the chat.')
194 def chat(model, build_mem):
195     """
196     chat: start an interactive chat with LLM to work on your ML project.
197     """
198     if not check_config(console):
199         return
200 
201     memory = LanceDBMemory(os.getcwd())
202     if build_mem:
203         working_dir = os.getcwd()
204         table_name = 'mle_chat_' + working_dir.split('/')[-1]
205         source_files = list_files(working_dir, ['*.py'])  # TODO: support more file types
206 
207         chunker = CodeChunker(os.path.join(working_dir, '.mle', 'cache'), 'py')
208         with Progress(
209                 SpinnerColumn(),
210                 TextColumn("[progress.description]{task.description}"),
211                 BarColumn(),
212                 TextColumn("[progress.percentage]{task.percentage:>3.0f}%"),
213                 TimeElapsedColumn(),
214                 console=console,
215         ) as progress:
216             process_task = progress.add_task("Processing files...", total=len(source_files))
217 
218             for file_path in source_files:
219                 raw_code = read_file(file_path)
220                 progress.update(
221                     process_task,
222                     advance=1,
223                     description=f"Adding {os.path.basename(file_path)} to memory..."
224                 )
225 
226                 chunks = chunker.chunk(raw_code, token_limit=100)
227                 memory.add(
228                     texts=list(chunks.values()),
229                     table_name=table_name,
230                     metadata=[{'file': file_path, 'chunk_key': k} for k, _ in chunks.items()]
231                 )
232 
233     return workflow.chat(os.getcwd(), model=model, memory=memory)

12     def __init__(self, project_path: str):
13         """
14         Memory: A base class for memory and external knowledge management.
15         Args:
16             project_path: the path to store the data.
17         """
18         self.db_name = '.mle'
19         self.table_name = 'memory'
20         self.client = lancedb.connect(uri=self.db_name)
21 
22         config = get_config(project_path)
23         if config["platform"] == "OpenAI":
24             self.text_embedding = get_registry().get("openai").create(api_key=config["api_key"])
25         else:
26             raise NotImplementedError
27 
28     def add(
29             self,
30             texts: List[str],
31             metadata: Optional[List[Dict]] = None,
32             table_name: Optional[str] = None,
33             ids: Optional[List[str]] = None,
34     ) -> List[str]:
35         """
36         Adds a list of text items to the specified memory table in the database.
37 
38         Args:
39             texts (List[str]): A list of text strings to be added.
40             metadata (Optional[List[Dict]]): A list of metadata to be added.
41             table_name (Optional[str]): The name of the table to add data to. Defaults to self.table_name.
42             ids (Optional[List[str]]): A list of unique IDs for the text items.
43                 If not provided, random UUIDs are generated.
44 
45         Returns:
46             List[str]: A list of IDs associated with the added text items.
47         """
48         if isinstance(texts, str):
49             texts = (texts,)
50 
51         if metadata is None:
52             metadata = [None, ] * len(texts)
53         elif isinstance(metadata, dict):
54             metadata = (metadata,)
55         else:
56             assert len(texts) == len(metadata)
57 
58         embeds = self.text_embedding.compute_source_embeddings(texts)
59 
60         table_name = table_name or self.table_name
61         ids = ids or [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(texts))]
62 
63         data = [
64             {
65                 "vector": embed,
66                 "text": text,
67                 "id": idx,
68                 "metadata": meta,
69             } for idx, text, embed, meta in zip(ids, texts, embeds, metadata)
70         ]
71 
72         if table_name not in self.client.table_names():
73             table = self.client.create_table(table_name, data=data)
74             table.create_fts_index("id")
75         else:
76             self.client.open_table(table_name).add(data=data)
77 
78         return ids
79 
80     def query(self, query_texts: List[str], table_name: Optional[str] = None, n_results: int = 5) -> List[List[dict]]:
81         """
82         Queries the specified memory table for similar text embeddings.
83 
84         Args:
85             query_texts (List[str]): A list of query text strings.
86             table_name (Optional[str]): The name of the table to query. Defaults to self.table_name.
87             n_results (int): The maximum number of results to retrieve per query. Default is 5.
88 
89         Returns:
90             List[List[dict]]: A list of results for each query text, each result being a dictionary with
91             keys such as "vector", "text", and "id".
92         """
93         table_name = table_name or self.table_name
94         table = self.client.open_table(table_name)
95         query_embeds = self.text_embedding.compute_source_embeddings(query_texts)
96 
97         results = [table.search(query).limit(n_results).to_list() for query in query_embeds]
98         return results
99 
100     def list_all_keys(self, table_name: Optional[str] = None):
101         """
102         Lists all IDs in the specified memory table.
103 
104         Args:
105             table_name (Optional[str]): The name of the table to list IDs from. Defaults to the instance's table name.
106 
107         Returns:
108             List[str]: A list of all IDs in the table.
109         """
110         table_name = table_name or self.table_name
111         table = self.client.open_table(table_name)
112         return [item["id"] for item in table.search(query_type="fts").to_list()]

114     def get(self, record_id: str, table_name: Optional[str] = None):
115         """
116         Retrieves a record by its ID from the specified memory table.
117 
118         Args:
119             record_id (str): The ID of the record to retrieve.
120             table_name (Optional[str]): The name of the table to query. Defaults to the instance's table name.
121 
122         Returns:
123             List[dict]: A list containing the matching record, or an empty list if not found.
124         """
125         table_name = table_name or self.table_name
126         table = self.client.open_table(table_name)
127         return table.search(query_type="fts") \
128             .where(f"id = '{record_id}'") \
129             .limit(1).to_list()
130 
131     def get_by_metadata(self, key: str, value: str, table_name: Optional[str] = None, n_results: int = 5):
132         """
133         Retrieves records matching a specific metadata key-value pair.
134 
135         Args:
136             key (str): The metadata key to filter by.
137             value (str): The value of the metadata key to filter by.
138             table_name (Optional[str]): The name of the table to query. Defaults to the instance's table name.
139             n_results (int): The maximum number of results to retrieve. Defaults to 5.
140 
141         Returns:
142             List[dict]: A list of records matching the metadata criteria.
143         """
144         table_name = table_name or self.table_name
145         table = self.client.open_table(table_name)
146         return table.search(query_type="fts") \
147             .where(f"metadata.{key} = '{value}'") \
148             .limit(n_results).to_list()

150     def delete(self, record_id: str, table_name: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
151         """
152         Deletes a record from the specified memory table.
153 
154         Args:
155             record_id (str): The ID of the record to delete.
156             table_name (Optional[str]): The name of the table to delete the record from. Defaults to self.table_name.
157 
158         Returns:
159             bool: True if the deletion was successful, False otherwise.
160         """
161         table_name = table_name or self.table_name
162         table = self.client.open_table(table_name)
163         return table.delete(f"id = '{record_id}'")
164 
165     def delete_by_metadata(self, key: str, value: str, table_name: Optional[str] = None):
166         """
167         Deletes records from the specified memory table based on a metadata key-value pair.
168 
169         Args:
170             key (str): The metadata key to filter by.
171             value (str): The value of the metadata key to filter by.
172             table_name (Optional[str]): The name of the table to delete records from. Defaults to the instance's table name.

174         Returns:

177         table_name = table_name or self.table_name

181     def drop(self, table_name: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
182         """
183         Drops (deletes) the specified memory table.
184 
185         Args:
186             table_name (Optional[str]): The name of the table to delete. Defaults to self.table_name.
187 
188         Returns:
189             bool: True if the table was successfully dropped, False otherwise.
190         """
191         table_name = table_name or self.table_name
192         return self.client.drop_table(table_name)

194     def count(self, table_name: Optional[str] = None) -> int:
195         """
196         Counts the number of records in the specified memory table.
197 
198         Args:
199             table_name (Optional[str]): The name of the table to count records in. Defaults to self.table_name.
200 
201         Returns:
202             int: The number of records in the table.
203         """
204         table_name = table_name or self.table_name
205         table = self.client.open_table(table_name)
206         return table.count_rows()
207 
208     def reset(self) -> None:
209         """
210         Resets the memory by dropping the default memory table.
211         """
212         self.drop()
